Messages.Author: Pete Johns
Messages.Body:
Hello! I've just realised the problem with Jyhad. I had been
playing no card limit for 2 years and bought loads of cards. I
had made two decks which were alright but there was always
some guy who would use a really boring deck and win. Then we
found this news group and started playing with the 'sensible'
rules given here. They were so confusing that we gave up
playing for a while as we were thoughrally dis illusioned.
Then my now good friend Mike came up and asked me if I wanted
a game under 4 card limit, naturally I thought he was joking
as Jyhad is meant to be played no limit. Still he persuaded me
to play and I found it incredible fun as there was no
confusing rules to think about and no degenerate decks I have
come across. I would just like to say that there would be less
need for this newsgroup if more people played a card limit. If
there is some degenerate decks under a card limit (and no
doubt there is) then perhaps it would be easier to ban those
deck concepts from tournements and not come up with a thousand
and one rule modifications. Just a thought....
PJ

I haven't been on here long, so please excuse me if I make a fool of
myself, but I felt the urge to respond to this post...

[previous arguments clipped]

[I took the liberty of clipping the first page or so as well, as they
argued primarily] [that VtES is not VtM and shouldn't be made as if it

Now hold on, you're saying two slightly different things here, and I
feel the distinction should be made. "Not everyone can create a
challenging deck using limited resources." I'm fine with that. I'd have
to agree that it's somewhat difficult to make a good deck under CL.
(I've played both CL and NL, so please don't tell me I don't know what
I'm talking about.) Your second comment, "This is the essence of Jyhad,
the ability to create a good deck," is equally harmless taken on its
own. I feel, however, that the two together make a faulty argument. I
agree that the essence of Jyhad is to make a good deck, but I do not see
why you think that the essence of the game is to make a good deck /under
CL/, which you seem to have implied. Please explain this.

> Card limit cuts out all but
> one degenerate deck (Malkavian S&B)

I played under 6CL for a time, and found that most of our table's combat
decks were surprisingly unaffected (The most notable were a Tremere
bleed+burn and a Gangrel aggro rush/diablerize/vote), so I have to
disagree with that comment, though I do agree that CL leaves a few decks
easily superior to most other "fun" or "theme" decks.

> but even that is stoppable
> in cases. By a minor modification such as you may only use a
> makimum of 4 malkavians in your deck would probably kill this
> tactic off all together

Whoa, whoa, whoa!!! It seems to me you're saying, "Jyhad's only a little
broken under CL: to fix it all you have to do is all-but-eliminate one
of the BASIC CLANS of the game?!?!" This, honestly, seems somewhat
ridiculous to me, especially if you take into account the large number
of pure-Malk decks that /aren't/ S&B. I've seen Malk vote, Malk combat,
and other weirder all-Malk decks that actually fared rather well, and
limiting the clan to 4 in the crypt, besides being against the nature of
the game, would destroy all of these alternate possibilities.

> plus in a competion where we are all
> trying to win, why not gang up on he who dares get out such a
> boring deck?

This "fix", on the other hand, contradicts the basic predator-prey
relationship that makes VtES different from a large MtG free-for-all. I
don't think it's fair to destroy the game in order to justify making
Jyhad more Magic-like!

> Just how popular is NL anyway? It seems to have
> a reasonable following in the States but I should add that I
> have played with many groups around Britain and have found
> that no player I have played with has played no limits, only a
> card limit of 4-6.

Not much to say about this, but I wanted to separate it from the next 2
comments for clarity's sake...

> This indicates to me that people prefere
> card limits in general as a better way to play.

Whoa, whoa, whoa (again)!!! It implies no such thing. When my group
played CL, we did so not because we thought it better, but because we
were used to playing Magic and saw no reason to do otherwise! Maybe try
asking some of your groups to play NL for a bit and see if they can
defeat Malk S&L /without/ destroying the basic elements of the game
(specifically, the predator-prey relationship and the near-banning of a
clan). If they like it, fine, if they still prefer CL, fine too, but
don't go /assuming/ that they prefer CL when they may not have even
considered the alternative.

> Perhaps we
> have more imagination here.....

> Gabriel

I'm just going to assume you were being sarcastic here, because
otherwise this comment could start an ungodly flame war that I don't
feel like dragging this newsgroup into.

-321(aka ben ranker)

On Thu, 24 Oct 1996, Lord of Shadows wrote:

> (L. Scott Johnson) wrote:

> But less then 4 in most cases.....

Assuming an _extremely_ small deck (60 cards), getting 2 Corruption cards
requires, on average, movement through just less than half the deck. This
reduces the use of Corruption to only reasonably useful on stealing 0-cost
allies, or 1 cost/capacity allies/vampires. Anything else is playing the
game _purely_ on luck.

> >>>Surely anyone can see that this card was designed to be used
> >>>in a no-limit environment.

[someone wrote:]
> >>[...] this card obviously requres more than four to steal larger

> >>vampires to make it effective in a single idea deck. But, that is what
> >>i think is the beauty of a 4cl, you cannot rely on just one card, you
> >> have to explore the clans strengths and weaknesses.

As you do with NL. A good-NL deck likely wouldn't make a "I'll corrupt
you" deck. It would probably lose. However, under CL, Corruption isn't
remotely useful, akin to using Illegal Search and Seizure, _hoping_ that
your opponents play expensive weapons, or when you know specifically that
you will be playing against weenies.

NL decks that rely on only 1 card have a name: One-Trick-Ponies (OTP).
They are often remarkably effective at their one-trick, but a OTP is at a
distint disadvantage in a general-NL environment because you need to be
prepared for _so_ much, and since most other decks build a broad based
defense (against 3 majors: bleed/vote/combat), their reliance on one card
makes them extremely succeptible to common defensive measures.

In describing the efficacy of the OTP in NL, I often use the following
analogy...
Decks in NL fall between two extremes, a long, wide board,
covering everything under neath it with minimal pressure when pressed
down, and a sharp pin, piercing deeply at times, but easily knocked over.

OTPs are notoriously erratic at winning. Decks constructed with even
standard defenses to the Big 3 strategies tend to have contingencies for
most things. When surprises do hit a deck, or when it becomes obvious a
deck has a weakness (as I found with one of my Fortitude based decks vs.
Tremere Combat, esp. Intercept Combat), they alter their deck to cover up
their holes. OTPs, by their very nature, either give up on covering up
their holes in favor of their tight, piercing nature, or they cover up the
holes and become more like that long, wide board.

> >With 4CL, IMHO, you get only a taste of the clan's strengths and
> >weaknesses (with the exception of Malkavians). To really explore
> >the strengths and weaknesses, you have to show a little more
> >focus.

> Not really, I think the strengths and weaknesses of most clans
> are apparent at any card limit. In 4 card limit if one
> discipline has a good card you cannot just rely on this to get
> the job done. It therefore allows more of the cards available
> to be used.

Not especially. Name a singular card you would rely on to "get the job
done". Majesty as combat defense? Weak against standard combat
anti-combat. Only Intercept against bleed? Weak against Seduction, Elder
Intervention. Misdirection to remove blockers? Wake and animalism become
defensive nightmares (so much lost pool, so little use). A broad defense
must be used, with focuses of more cards (perhaps 4, but perhaps 8 or 10)
where they are useful for your deck, but alternatives with fewer cards in
case someone is prepared for your aproach. Most good decks have to spread
out their card usage, allowing more of the cards avaiable to be used.

> The downside to this however is if Wizards of the
> coast (in there infinate wisdom...?) bring out many cards which
> are the same under different names then it effectively gives
> some disciplines the advantage of having an equivelent of 8
> cards of the same.

But they have already done this. Note Stealth and Intercept and their
amount of repetition in the card set. Then note, most animalism cards are
not repeated. Most Serpentis/Necro/Vote/Protean are not.

> In no limit if one disipline has a good card
> you could just use that repeatedly (such as traps instead of
> conquer the beast) and not have to look for alternatives. This
> may not necessarily be a bad thing as the variety of decks you
> can create EASILY will be increased but the challenge of deck
> creation is lessened. Thats the main reason I play card limits
> and beleive it is this extra challenge that has created the
> breakaway group of card limiters. Still, each to there own as
> there are many merits to both sides of the game....

I agree that there does exist a challenge in making viable decks in
4CL, but the problem I find is with the total 4CL environment. This
challenge is not equal accrossed the board. There is no hinderence at all
for a Sneak and Bleed deck in 4CL. However, making a decent vote deck or
rush deck takes a lot more work to even be passably viable. The
environment itself is unbalanced towards one strategy, and _that_ is what
I don't like.

Comparing challenge of deck creation is relatively useless, as they are
different styles of deck creation. With 4CL, the challenge basicly comes
in finding how to overcome the CL itself, but deck design is made somewhat
easier. In NL, making a similar deck as designed in CL requires much more
thought. In a rush deck that needs, say 10 to 15 get into combat cards,
for example, you can't just thow in 4 Bum's Rush, 4 Haven Uncovered, 2-3
Sports Bikes, and 4 Contracts (for Assamites). Maybe the deck would be
better of with 8 Contracts and 6 Bum's Rushes. Maybe the deck would be
best with 6 Haven Uncovered, 4 Sport Bike and 2 Contracts. Maybe the deck
is best with 4 of each. But you have to understand the differences of
each to put them in.

Gue...@msn.com (Anthony McBride) wrote:

>nothing wrong with card limits! (esp to prevent sick cards such as
>'thoughts betrayed' being used to excess)

Neither the rule book, nor the official tournament rules mention
anything about card limits. Therefore, it is not good enough for
there to be "nothing wrong with card limits" ( which is debatable ).
There must be something _good_ about card limits. There must
be an observed problem in the game, which card limits fix. Card
limits must somehow make the game more enjoyable. It is not
good enough for it to simply _not_ make the game _less_
enjoyable.

As for it supposedly fixing spoiler cards (such as thoughts
betrayed):

1) It does not fix "sick cards such as thoughts betrayed".
The cards still do the same thing they did before,
you just draw them less often. Thoughts betrayed
is still "sick". Since these cards are still more useful
and powerful then other cards, it becomes important
to have the maximum allowed in every deck. Many
of us saw this happen in M:tG. I've never seen a
tournament level M____ deck without all five moxen,
and a lotus ( and usually the time cards ). That's why
I don't play M:t$ any more, and I don't want to see
it happen to V:tES.

2) Let's forget about thoughts betrayed for a minute (it's special
in various ways, and isn't a very good example). Before
SPTR/GT, freak drive was often thought of as a spoiler
card. It allowed one minion take large numbers of bleed
actions in one turn, and this was unbalanced. Some
players thought that a four card limit would fix this
problem. If you can only have four freak drives in your
deck, you can still bleed multiple times in one turn, with
one minion, which is still unbalanced, but you can't do it
very often. And then they printed force of will, and rutor's
hand, and card limits don't work so well any more. There
will likely be more similar cards in Sabbat, and future
expansions, and card limits will work less, and less well.

3) WotC does not support card limits, and the cards sets they
design will not be designed to function correctly in a
card limit environment.

4) Why are flash, and undead strenght limited to four each?
because thoughts betrayed is unabalanced? That's
very unfair to any players that can't afford to get the
expensive rares to replace the useful ( and balanced )
commons that you wont let them play with.

Larrx...
